target_customer: Initially telehealth and mental health companies buying clinician hours; now patients, who pay or use insurance, for psychiatric care
problem: Shortage of mental health professionals; psychiatric care is administratively heavy and expensive to deliver.
business_model: Direct-care psychiatry practice with AI-automated operations (marketplace for clinician hours at launch)

founders.name: Yash Patel
prior_employers: Harvard Medical School (research assistant, per profile)
founders.background_notes: Worked on Medicare and Medicaid payment policy at CBO

competitors.name: Cerebral
competitors.what: VC-backed direct-to-consumer telehealth for mental health

technical_complexity.rationale: 2021 marketplace was standard engineering; the later AI-native care platform and regulated AI prescribing are much harder.

defensibility.rationale: Marketplace had little defensibility; Utah regulatory authorization for AI prescription renewals (April 2026) is a differentiating position, though Doctronic holds similar Utah authority.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Direct-to-consumer players were funded in 2021 but did not absorb the marketplace wedge; Legion left the marketplace model itself.

market_need_then: At the 2021 launch the founders cited a shortage of 230,000+ US mental health professionals; initial network was 131 professionals matched manually (HN launch post as mirrored).

identity.voice_and_tone: Founders frame messaging around AI-native care ('from humans to tokens')

branding.community_and_virality: Press about the Utah AI-prescribing authorization (Verge, Bloomberg Law, PYMNTS, April 2026) concerns the product, not the brand

brand_strength.rationale: Name is short and clean but no source shows brand-driven pull; press attention is about the regulatory milestone.

pivots.from: Marketplace selling psychiatrist and therapist time to telehealth companies
pivots.why: CEO said they deeply understood the provider experience; one account says the marketplace would not reach their goals (bhbusiness headline dates the pivot to Oct 2024)

outcome_analysis: Legion Health started as a manual staffing marketplace for mental health in 2021, then pivoted by 2024 into running its own AI-enabled psychiatry practice and raised a $6.3M seed. In April 2026 Utah cleared its AI to renew certain psychiatric prescriptions, a regulatory first-mover edge. It is still Active with a small team, so the outcome is unresolved.
notes: Seed round confirmed by two outlets (HIT Consultant, Behavioral Health Business headline) but no investors or post-money named. Unverified and conflicting: $2M seed March 2022, totals $8.3M, $10M, $16M (Dealroom/Caplight), job posts say $6.3M then $23M raised. HN launch is read via a blog mirror. hitconsultant calls the company Austin-based while YC lists San Francisco. Name origin not found.
